verdicts.evidence: The open call reads the expanded pip configuration path inside a try whose read failures return without an index URL.
Opening the configuration must succeed before get_index can return the nonempty URL required to pass the early return.
The condition concerns availability of a specific user configuration artifact.
The tested line comes from readlines on the file opened as the user pip configuration.
A line must contain index-url to supply the URL used by the guarded commands.
This tests a substring in configuration file content.
The branch condition directly tests membership in sys.argv.
The wheel-handling body runs when bdist_wheel is present in sys.argv.
The argument identifies the package build command being requested.
The expression omits the requirement that the extracted URL be nonempty: a readable file containing a line ending with index-url= satisfies c1 and c2 but returns an empty string and exits.
The early return disables the pip install command when no index URL is available.
The URL availability check activates installation when configuration is available, without checking for analysis tools.
Data_availability fits better: the configuration supplies the index URL interpolated into pip install, and absence of that input returns early.
The subprocess call lies directly in the region after the no-index early return.
The sink is inside the nested callback after its URL guard; registering the callback at exit does not bypass that guard.
The resolved subprocess.check_output invokes pip install through the shell, which can download a package and execute installation code.
Even with bdist_wheel present, a readable configuration with an empty index-url value satisfies the listed conditions but exits; the conjunction omits the nonempty extracted URL requirement.
The guards enable the download and wheel replacement operations.
The configuration and command checks activate wheel handling for the matching invocation.
Portability fits better: the build-command check adapts wheel download and placement to bdist_wheel, using the configured index as input.
All three sinks lie after the URL early return and inside the bdist_wheel body, including the nested directory branches.
The download, move and unlink sites are local to the callback and cannot be reached there without passing both cited guards.
The subprocess command runs pip download, shutil.move writes the destination artifact, and os.unlink deletes the existing artifact.
